item.title: Show HN: Executable Markdown files with Unix pipes
item.description:
I wanted to run markdown files like shell scripts. Tasks that needed LLM orchestration libraries are now markdown files composed with standard Unix tools. Install scripts like `curl -fsSL https://bun.

HN Discussion

Read Original Article

Top 4 Comments:

brandonkal:

This is cool. Executable markdown files are an underutilized concept.

I built https://github.com/brandonkal/inkjet to make building CLIs super simple. All of my private repos have an inkjet.md file for common tasks and documentation. I use code blocks for the executable section and the language determines the runtime. I realize now inkjet could be extended to support an LLM executor by default. PRs welcome.

signalnine:

lmao nondeterministic shell scripting

chrismorgan:

I get the intent, but it’s bizarre to hear invocation of nondeterministic tools that occasionally delete people’s entire drives “more auditable”.

serious_angel:

Oh dear... but... but why let some LLM set of unknown source of unknown iteration... execute code... in your machine...?

I was excited in the possibly extravagant implementation idea and... when I read enough to realize it's based on some yet another LLM... Sorry, no, never. You do you.

item.title: Logistics Is Dying; Or – Dude, Where's My Mail?
item.description:
Russell established the Overland Express Route, colloquially called the Pony Express, to carry express mail between St. The mail stopped working. 6% of first-class mail on time.

HN Discussion

Read Original Article

Top 1 Comments:

GuB-42:

When "free shipping" is what consumers expect, do you think people are ready to pay for better service? It the package is lost, it is often cheaper to write it off as a loss and send another item or refund.

If you need overnight shipping, you can have it, but it is not cheap, so most people won't do it. As for documents, is is all electronic now.

Logistics is very much alive, but it is adapted to our needs, that is massive containerships for worldwide trade, local warehouses for fast delivery of common items, reliability that is in balance with the cost of losing items, speed matching what people are ready to pay for, and specialized services for special needs, like overnight shipping.
